BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

# Legal Memorandum: Review of Seller’s Draft SPA & Disclosure Letter (Project Kestrel)

**To:** Amelia Frost & Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team  
**From:** AI Legal Assistant (Buyer Deal Team Counsel)  
**Date:** March 30, 2026  
**Subject:** Review of Seller (Harbourglass Ventures) Draft SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

---

### Executive Summary

The Seller’s updated draft SPA and Disclosure Letter depart significantly from the Wattlebridge Holdings Negotiating Playbook across almost every key risk-allocation and liability area. 

The Seller has attempted to:
1. Standardise and compress warranty caps, de minimis levels, and time limits into a single seller-favourable bucket.
2. Apply general liability caps and time limits to Fundamental/Title, Tax, and IP claims.
3. Apply blanket limitations, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance clauses across all claims without carving out **fraud, wilful concealment, or deliberate misconduct**.
4. Rely on whole-data-room and public-register general disclosures to neutralise warranty protections.
5. Soften critical closing conditions (Bluefen) and debt/security release mechanisms (Riverlark Bank).
6. Omit the DD-005 employee completion bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs) from the completion funds flow.

Below is a detailed legal analysis of the departures, our rationale for rejection, and actionable mark-up recommendations.

---

### Detailed Analysis of Departures & Pushback Rationale

#### 1. General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)
* **Seller Draft:** General liability cap set at 20% of the Purchase Price (AUD 4,800,000).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Starting position is **25% (AUD 6,000,000)**. A fallback to 20% is strictly conditional upon prior written authorisation from Amelia Frost identifying the specific draft (no such authority has been granted).
* **Pushback:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000 in the draft mark-up.

#### 2. Claim Thresholds & De Minimis (Clause 12.2)
* **Seller Draft:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; aggregate basket of AUD 250,000; recoverable on an "excess-only" (deductible) basis.
* **Playbook Mandate:** De minimis of **AUD 5,000**; aggregate basket of **AUD 50,000**; recoverable on a **first-dollar (tipping basket)** basis once exceeded.
* **Pushback:** Reduce de minimis to AUD 5,000, reduce aggregate threshold to AUD 50,000, and convert the basket mechanism to first-dollar recovery.

#### 3. General Time Limits (Clause 12.3 / 13)
* **Seller Draft:** 18-month notification period for General Warranty Claims, applying globally across all claims unless expressly stated.
* **Playbook Mandate:** **24 months** after Completion for General Warranties (18 months requires Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been provided).
* **Pushback:** Extend general warranty limitation period to 24 months after Completion. Reject any default application of general limitation periods to non-general claim categories.

#### 4. Fundamental & Title Claims (Clauses 9.3, 12, Schedule 7)
* **Seller Draft:** Title, capacity, and fundamental warranties subject to the general 20% cap, 18-month time limit, general basket, and knowledge bars.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Title and fundamental claims must be subject to a **separate regime**: **100% cap (Purchase Price)**, at least **6 years** notification period, and fully carved out from the general basket, de minimis, and buyer knowledge bars.
* **Pushback:** Re-establish a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime with a 100% cap, 6-year claim window, and zero threshold/knowledge restrictions.

#### 5. Fraud, Wilful Concealment & Deliberate Misconduct (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
* **Seller Draft:** Limitation caps, exclusive-remedy clauses, and non-reliance provisions apply to *all* claims of any nature without exception.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be **carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance clauses** to the maximum extent permitted by law.
* **Pushback:** Insert explicit, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment carve-outs across all limitation, remedy, and non-reliance provisions.

#### 6. Disclosure Regime & Data Room Blanket Disclosure (Schedule 7 & Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
* **Seller Draft:** General disclosure of the entire indexed electronic data room (DD-002 to DD-012), corporate registers, and public records.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Reject whole-data-room, public-register, and prudent-search deemed disclosures. Require **specific fair disclosure** (facts fully and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify nature and scope).
* **Pushback:** Delete general data-room and public-register deeming provisions from the SPA and Disclosure Letter; mandate specific, fair disclosure standards.

#### 7. Buyer Knowledge Exclusion (Clause 8.3)
* **Seller Draft:** Complete bar on claims if Buyer or its advisers had actual or constructive knowledge (including matters discoverable from data room or public records).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any seller-knowledge qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge individuals after reasonable enquiry, and knowledge qualifiers must **never** excuse Title, Capacity, Fraud, or Specific Indemnity claims.
* **Pushback:** Remove general buyer knowledge bars. Qualify Seller warranties only by the actual knowledge of specified individual Seller officers after reasonable inquiry.

#### 8. Bluefen Consent Condition (Clauses 3 & 6.3; Disclosure Letter Item 2)
* **Seller Draft:** "Reasonable endeavours" standard; condition deemed satisfied merely upon delivery of counterparty written consent.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Bluefen accounts for ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). Requires **effective consent AND evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied prior to Completion**. "Reasonable endeavours" and simple delivery of a letter are inadequate.
* **Pushback:** Require an express, non-waivable Condition Precedent (CP) for Bluefen consent, including verified satisfaction of all underlying conditions under clause 11.3 prior to Completion.

#### 9. Riverlark Bank Facility & Security Discharge (Clauses 2 & 7; Disclosure Letter Item 3)
* **Seller Draft:** Post-completion release of facility (~AUD 3.2m outstanding) and security.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Facility must be fully paid out at Completion via direct payment from Completion funds, with effective security releases provided at Completion. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's express written approval.
* **Pushback:** Require direct repayment out of closing funds at Completion and delivery of executed release documents (or bank-issued irrevocable undertakings to release upon payout).

#### 10. Employee Completion Bonuses & On-Costs (Funds Flow & Disclosure Letter Item 5)
* **Seller Draft:** DD-005 completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) treated as a "matter for the Seller" and omitted from the draft Completion funds flow, omitting payroll tax, superannuation, and on-costs.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Bonuses (AUD 420,000) plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) must be an explicit line-item deduction in the funds flow or fully funded by the Seller prior to Completion.
* **Pushback:** Insert explicit line-item deduction in the Completion Funds Flow covering the AUD 420,000 bonus pool plus all associated employer on-costs (superannuation/payroll tax).

#### 11. Ironquay IP Indemnity (Clause 11.1 & Disclosure Letter Item 4)
* **Seller Draft:** Indemnity restricted narrowly to SOW3 payment. AUD 180,000 open fee in DD-010 is unverified by bank records.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Broaden the indemnity to cover all IP ownership risks and third-party claims arising from Ironquay development, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.
* **Pushback:** Expand Clause 11.1 into a full indemnity covering any IP ownership challenge or fee dispute from Ironquay, maintaining SOW3 cure mechanics and ensuring Buyer isn't exposed to unverified fee claims.

#### 12. Export / Data Privacy Incident (DD-006 & Disclosure Letter Item 6)
* **Seller Draft:** Characterised as a preliminary operational matter and not expected to be material.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Treat with caution without making unverified assumptions. Require Seller to preserve logs, conduct thorough investigation, and provide regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, or duty until investigation concludes.
* **Pushback:** Include covenants requiring log preservation, prompt delivery of forensic updates, and appropriate indemnity coverage should the incident result in third-party claims or regulatory action.

#### 13. Sandbar Supplier Renewals (DD-008, DD-011 & Disclosure Letter Item 8)
* **Seller Draft:** Disclosed as ordinary-course operating costs (AUD 330,000 aggregate).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Assess operational terms without automatically classifying as Debt or making immediate price deductions unless justified by DD terms.
* **Pushback:** Conduct contractual review of the renewal terms to confirm ordinary-course status and ensure no accrued liabilities or onerous lock-in provisions exist.

#### 14. Tax & IP Regime Separation
* **Seller Draft:** Considers Tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime and general caps.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Keep Title, Tax, IP, and Payment categories separate. Tax and IP terms remain OPEN. Tax must be covered under a standalone Tax Indemnity (uncapped or specific cap) and extended limitation period.
* **Pushback:** Carve Tax and IP out of the general liability caps/regime into dedicated schedules/indemnities.

#### 15. Independent Title Verification (Disclosure Letter Item 10)
* **Seller Draft:** Title to 100% shares relies solely on internal Company share register (DD-012).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Internal registers are supplied internal sources, not independent legal proof.
* **Pushback:** Require independent verification, title warranties, and encumbrance searches prior to Completion.

---

### Summary of Recommendations for SPA Mark-Up

| Issue Area |
